requirements: Every machine needs git, a POSIX sh (git's) and Python 3.11 or later on PATH. Without them, onFailure "block" refuses every matched tool call on that machine.
onFailure needs Claude Code 2.1.295 or later; an older client lets a crashed or timed-out hook through.
The bundle must sit at deploy_root exactly: the hook commands name it by absolute path.
caveats: Managed settings bind Claude Code only. A local administrator can edit or delete these files.
On WSL, /etc/claude-code is writable by the user as well.
By default (managedSourcesBehavior "first-wins") a machine that also receives server-managed or MDM policy skips the managed settings files without a warning; /status names the source in use.
onFailure has no effect on Stop hooks, so the turn-end gate fails open when it crashes.
A file in managed-settings.d that is not valid JSON stops Claude Code from starting.
The labels are vendor-docs evidence, unwitnessed: nobody has watched this file refuse a call yet.
claude_code.lock_note: --lock adds allowManagedHooksOnly: every user, project and plugin hook on the machine stops running, chock's own project hooks and plugins included.
claude_code.never_note: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly is never emitted: it would discard every user and project permission rule.
